newsitem.title: USA: BPA raises firm peak power by $1/MWh for Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: BPA raises firm peak power by $1/MWh for Tuesday.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) raised prices for firm power during peak demand hours on Tuesday by $1.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Monday.

BPA offered up to 500 MW of firm, peak power for Monday at $13.00 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $14.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales, up from $12.00 and $13.00, respectively, for Monday.
Tuesday firm off-peak prices were unchanged at $10.50 per MWh for all deliveries.
Up to 500 MW of non-firm power for hours ending 0800-1000 and 1800-2000 PST on Monday was offered at $15.00 (Northwest) and $16.00 (COB), unchanged from Monday prices.
Non-firm power during shoulder hours (0700, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200) was offered at $13.00 (Northwest) and $14.00 (COB), up about $1.50 per MWh from Monday.
Non-firm power during off-peak hours on Tuesday was offered at $10.50 for all deliveries.
BPA also offered displacement power during off-peak hours on Tuesday at $7.00 and $9.00 per MWh.
